tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when a training job is denied access...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (fails, hangs, denied access, capacity errors, hidden loss metrics) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name components by name ('even if they do not mention execution roles, key policies...'), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of memory... even if they do not mention execution roles, key policies, checkpoint paths, metric definitions, security groups or data channels by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays domain-specific throughout — it does not explain what SageMaker, S3, or training jobs are in general terms, but instead focuses on project-specific check-ids, API quirks, and routing logic the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: "Grounded in the LLM-SM check family under checks-sagemaker-training.md" — the content jumps directly into check-ids, severities, and read-only API behaviors without general background explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains index tables (what-it-catches, router) that point to references/ for full detail rather than embedding the full detection rules, remediations, or citations inline. Conditional branches (Router, Review Procedure) link out to references instead of inlining detailed data.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.
tests.evidence: "[checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md)", "[collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md)", "[metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md)", "[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md)", "[known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md)" all appear linked in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by explicit conditions for when to load it, e.g. tied to symptom matches, specific steps, or check-id assignment.
tests.evidence: "load it before assigning any check-id or severity" and "load it whenever the user names a specific error or symptom" demonstrate clear load conditions for each reference.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.
tests.evidence: "[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md)" and similar relative-path links throughout the body.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations like the Review Procedure and Guardrails are prescriptive with explicit ordered checklists and non-negotiable rules, while flexible areas like how to phrase findings or choose remediation commands leave room for agent judgment. The balance matches operation fragility.
tests.evidence: "Guardrails ... Non-negotiable, at every step" vs. "Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it" shows calibrated prescriptiveness without over-specifying every phrasing.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal options; it specifies exact AWS APIs per use case in the Router table without unnecessary alternatives.
tests.evidence: Router table: "DescribeTrainingJob FailureReason, then the JSONL sample" — a single clear path per symptom rather than a menu of alternatives.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable diagnostic approach (classify, bucket, confirm, disclose) applicable to any training job, rather than describing one specific job instance.
tests.evidence: "Classify before prescribing anything... track progress against this checklist" describes a reusable procedure applicable across any job, not a one-off declaration.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has dedicated 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' sections documenting non-obvious API quirks and misconceptions specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: "'The job is InProgress with Pending, so it is failing.' A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not Failed."
